endorsements.quote: Fourth, for safe and sustainable AI adoption, health workers would require training so they can effectively interact with AI tools.
This would necessitate development of clear frameworks to define liability for any adverse events when AI systems are used in patient care.
Fifth, AI facilitated work force productivity and deployments should not exacerbate inequalities, therefore marginalized populations such as those in rural areas should be prioritized.

unlisted_practices: Conduct cost-effectiveness analyses comparing AI-enabled task-shifting with traditional care before adopting AI interventions in low-income settings.
Conduct discrete choice experiments to elicit patient, health worker, and policymaker preferences on AI integration to inform policy and investment decisions.
Establish strong data protection, privacy, and ethical-use systems with data oversight and governance.
Develop guidelines for integrating AI into human resources for health planning and deployment, treating AI as a complement to workforce development rather than a substitute.
Include rigorous monitoring of outcomes, costs, acceptance, and unintended consequences in AI implementations.
Circumscribe AI replacement of human providers to specific conditions and contexts where safety, affordability, and efficiency are assured.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/commentary paper discussing the opportunities, policy implications, and governance of task-shifting and AI integration into health systems in Malawi.
